 Present: Dhanesh Mugali
 B.Com., LL.B.,(Spl.)

 Member, Mact

 S/o Venkatappa,
 Aged about 41 years

 Mallappanahalli road,
 Muttugadahalli,
 Shivakote,

 Respondents 1.  Sri.Chyinta Chakradhara  Rao, S/o Venkatarathnam,

 Ramalingeshwara Nagar,
 Vijayawada Urban,
 Andhra Pradesh - 520013  (RC Owner of the Lorry  bearing No.AP-16/TW-3587)
 (By Pleader Sri P.
 Niranjuan Rao)

1  2. The New India Assurance  Co. ltd., T.P.Hub, 2nd floor,
 Mahalakshmi Chamb ers,
 M.G.Road, Bangalore 01  (Policy No.
 62080031200100001379)
 valid from 11-6-2020 to 10-  06-2021) 
 (By Pleader Sri S.V.
 Sudhakar Reddy) 
 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident. 
The brief facts of the Petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 1-1-20221 at about 2-45 a.m. the petitioner was driving the TATA Ace bearing Reg.No.KA- 05/AF-4666 with other occupants, on Kolar - Bangalore road, NH-75, when he reached near Gangapura gate, at that time driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587 parked the same in the center of the road negligently without showing any signal or indicator. As result of which, the Petitioner dashed the said Lorry from behind and sustained grievous injuries. 
3. It is further stated that, immediately the Petitioner was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital, Hosakote,
for first aid, then he was shifted to M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy and working as a Driver and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. After the accident, he could not do any work as prior to the accident. 
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587. Hence, Nandagudi Police have filed a case against driver of said vehicle. As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the Petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation. 
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents. In response to the notices,
the Respondent No.1 & 2 appeared through their respective Counsels and filed the Written statements. 
Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
2 7. Brief averments of the Written statement of the Respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case. Further, he has stated that he is the RC Owner of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587 and he got insured said vehicle with respondent No.2. As on the date of the accident the policy was in force, hence respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1. But, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner only, as the driver of Lorry had parked the vehicle with safety measures i..e, parking lights. Hence, he is not liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner. 
8. Brief averments of the Written statement of the Respondent No.2 are as under:
The Respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case. Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of Insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587 and restricted its liability subject to terms and conditions of the policy. Further it has stated that,
the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence, Permit and FC to the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy. The petitioner drove his vehicle under the influence of alcohol in a rash and negligent by carrying more persons than the permitted seating capacity and caused the accident. Hence, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties. 
Further, both respondents have denied the age, income and avocation of the Petitioner and expenses incurred towards medical and other incidental charges. 
Further they have contended that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive,
exaggerated and arbitrary. With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost. 
9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in an motor vehicle accident, that was taken place on 01-01-2021 at about 2-45 a.m. near Gangapura gate, Kolar - Bangalore road, NH-75, due to the rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing Reg.No.AP16/TW-3587? 
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award? 
Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
3 10. In order to substantiate his case, the Petitioner has got examined as Pw.1 and has also got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and have got marked in all 17 documents, marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
11. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has got examined its Assistant as Rw.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R1. The Respondent No.1 did not adduce the oral or documentary evidence. 
12. Heard the arguments of from both the learned Counsel and perused the materials available on record.
13. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following: 
R E A S O N S 14. ISSUE No.1:- The Petitioner has filed this petition against respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a accident that occurred due to sole negligent act of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587.
15. The main contention of the Respondents is that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Petitioner and Charge sheet is filed against the Petitioner. Hence, they are not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 
16. In order to prove his case, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW1. In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition. Further he has got marked 11 documents as Ex.P1 to 11. Ex.P1-Copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2- Copy of Complaint,
Ex.P3-Copy of Spot mahazar. Ex . P4 -Copy of spot sketch. Ex.P5-Copy of IMV report, Ex.P6-Copy of wound certificate, Ex.P7-Copy of Discharge summary, Ex.P8-Medical bills, Ex.P9 - Notarized copy of the Aadhaar card, Ex.P10-Notarized copy of the D.L. card and Ex.P11-Copy of Charge sheet. 
17. On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined its Assistant as RW1. RW.1 in his chief affidavit he has reiterated the entire contents of the written statement. Further he has got marked Ex.R1. Ex.R1 is the authorization letter. 
18. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the Complaint given by one Sri.Puttaraju, the S.H.O. of Nandagudi Police has registered the case against the Petitioner as A1 and driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 & 304(A) of I.P.C. After completion of investgation the police has filed charge sheet against petitioner and driver of Lorry bearing No. AP-16-TW-3581 for the offence punishable U/Sec. 279,
337 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec. 122 of MV Act respectively. 
Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
4 19. In the Cross examination of Pw.1, he has admitted that the accident spot is 30 feet width High way. Further he has admitted that he is also accused as per Charge sheet. Except this nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to prove that, accident was occurred only due to his rash and negligent driving. 
20. On perusal of Spot sketch it appears that TATA Ace vehicle dashed to the lorry from back side at mid night. As per Charge sheet the Petitioner drove his vahicle in a rash and negligent manner on Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 road, near Gangapura gate dashed Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587,
which was parked by his driver without giving any signal or indicator. After completion of investigatin the Nandagudi Police have filed charge sheet against Petitioner as A1 for the offence punishable U/sec.279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC and driver of offending vehicle as A2, for the offence punishable U/sec.122 of IMV Act. On going through the Police documents and answers given by the PW1 and RW1 it is crystal clear that, this accident occurred due to negligent act on the part of the driver of the Lorry and, rash and negligent driving of the Petitioner. 
21. The learned counsel for petitioner has argued that accident was occured due to sole negligence act of driver of Lorry bearing No. AP-16-TW-3587. Because the driver of the lorry ought to have taken some precations while parking the vehilce on the road. Six MVC petitions had been disposed by this court which arose out of same accident. In those petitions contributory negligency has been fixed on driver of Lorry and petitioner in the ration of 85% and 15% respectively and has requested to apply same ratio in this petition also. Further, learned cousel for petitioner has argued that under same facts of the cases our Hon'ble High Court and Hon'ble Apex Court have fixed the liability on the driver who parked the vehicle without taking precautions. 
22. The Counsel for the Petitoner has relied upon following citations:
a) Royal Sundaram Gen.Ins.Co. Ltd., V/s Savita and others. 2017 (4) AKR 200.
b) Kumari Jyothi and Others., V/s Mohd. Usman Ali and others ILR 2002 kar 893.
I have gone through the supra decisinos the principle laid down in the supra decision is that, the negligence could be attributed only to the driver of the lorry in view of the provision of Sec.122 of IMV Act. In this case also, the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.AP- 16/TW-3587 was parked on the road at night without signals. Admittedly, accident was happened at about 2- 45 a.m. by applying the principle laid down in the supra decisions , it can be held that, due to negligency of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587 accident was occurred. But this court had fixed contributory negligency on the petitioner as well as driver of the Lorry bearing No. AP-16-TW-3587 in MVC petition No.747/2021, 748/2021, 1085/2021, 1086/2021 and 1090/2021 which arose out of same accident. In this petition the respondent have not adduced any fresh evidence, except examination of its Assistant as RW-1. In his cross examinaiton he denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for petitioner. Admittedly, this witness is not an eye witness. Further, police records speak that the petitioner and driver of Lorry are accused in charge sheet. After careful scrutiny of Police documents i.e., FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, IMV report, Wound certificate,
Charge sheet, and in the light of the evidence placed by Petitioner, I am of the view that, the accident Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
5 was occurred due to Contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and also due to negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle. Hence, contributory negligence is taken on the part of the Driver of offending Lorry at 85% and also on the part of the Petitioner at 15%. Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative. 
23. ISSUE No.2: This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner. The Petitioner through this petition, claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads. 
24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the Petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act. 
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. 
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant. The compensation should not be assessed conservatively. On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency. The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner." "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable. That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment. But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation." 
Pain and Sufferings: As per Ex.P6 Wound certificate issued by M.S.Ramaiah Hospital, the Petitioner has sustained the following injuries:-
1. injury to left thigh.
2. Multiple facial abrasion and cut lacerated wound over the chin and Cut lacerated wound below left knee. 
The doctor opined that the injury No.1 is grevious and Injury No.2 is simple in nature. Hence, by considering the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner and opinion of the doctor, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings. 
Loss of income during treatment period:
25. The Petitioner has stated that, he was working as Driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. In this regard, he has not placed any document to prove his actual income. On going through Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
6 the Ex.P7 discharge summary, the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in M.S.Ramaiah hospital from 01-01-2021 to 05-01-2021 for about 5 days. During the period of treatment, definitely,
there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him. Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period. 
Medical Expeneses:
26. The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P8. The respondents have not disputed the said bills produced by the Petitioner. There is no contradiction to disbelieve the bills produced by the Petitoner. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.24,201/- towards medical expenses. 
Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
27. On going through the Ex.P7 discharge summary, the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in M.S.Ramaiah hospital from 01-01-2021 to 05-01- 2021 for about 5 days, so definitely the Petitioner would have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges. Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
Loss of future income: 
28. To prove the assessment of disability, the Petitioner got examined Doctor B.N.Nagaraj as PW-3. 
In the chief examination affidavit the doctor deposed that, on 15.2.2024 the Petitioner approached him for assessment of disability purpose. On examination, he found that, the Petitioner has healed scar over the left thigh, restricted left hip and knee movements with wasting of the left thigh muscles. Recent X-ray of the left femur shows united fractures with implant in situ. Further, he assessed the total disability to the left lower limb at 47% and for whole body of the Petitioner at 16%. 
29. In the Cross examination doctor has admitted that, he has not treated the Petitioner, Petitioner visited to him only for getting disability Certificate, fracture is united and after removal of implant there is a chance of decrease of disability. However by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal had taken the disability of the Petitioner at 15% to the whole body. 
30. The Petitioner has stated that, he was working as Driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. In this regard, he has not placed any document to prove his actual income. In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration. This accident had taken place in the year 2021. As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021. 
Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
7 31. As per Ex.P10 Copy of D.L. card, the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 04-04-1979. This accident occurred in the year 2021. Therefore, age of the Petitioner is considered as 42 years at the time of accident. Then the proper multiplier applicable is 14 which comes as follows:
Rs.15,000 x 12 x 14 x 15% = Rs.3,78,000/-
Hence, this tribunal awarded Rs.3,78,000/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
32. Towards future medication the PW.3 Doctor deposed in his chief examination affidavit that, the Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant, the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-. Neither the Petitioner, nor the doctor have produced the estimation for future surgery/ medication of the Petitioner. However, by considering the documents, nature of injury and evidence of doctor this tribunal awarded Rs.30,000/- under the head future medical expenses which does not carry any interest. 
33. The Petitioner sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury as shown in the wound certificate. As per Ex.P7 discharge summary he took treatment in the hospital for about 5 days, In the chief examination affidavit the Petitioner deposed that, due to accidental injuries he is unable to walk, sit, squat, climb stairs, and do any work as prior to the accident, hence by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and condition of the petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities. 
34. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
Towards loss of income during laid Rs. 15,000/-
up period Medical expenses Rs. 24,201/-
Transportation, Nourishment,
Conveyance and attendant Rs. 10,000/-
charges.
Loss of future income due to Rs. 3,78,000/-
disability Towards future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Towards loss of amenities of life Rs. 30,000/-
 Total Rs. 5,37,201/-
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,37,201/-. 
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,37,201/- along with interest @ 6%
per annum, as per the preposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in the case Rajugowda vs Chinta Chakradhara Rao on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137758054/
8 of MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018. And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, 
till the realization of the award amount. 
35. Liability:-
As per the Petition, the Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner & Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587. As already discussed in the issue no.1 and it is proved that, the accident occurred due to contributory negligence on the part of the Petitioner and also due to negligent act of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-16/TW-3587. But major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the Lorry and some contributory negligence is taken on the Petitioner. 
Hence, contributory negligence of 85% is taken on the part of the driver of the Lorry and 15% is taken on the part of the Petitioner. It is already held that the petitioner is entitled for total award amount of Rs.5,37,201/- out of it respondent No.1 and 2 have to pay 85% of the award amount of Rs.5,37,201/- which would be Rs.4,56,621/-.
36. As per records, Insurance policy of Lorry bearing No.AP-16-TW-3587 was valid from 11.06.2020 to 10.06.2021. The accident occurred on 01.01.2021. Hence, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of 85% i.e., Rs.4,56,621/- as discussed above with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization. Remaining 15% i.e., Rs.80,580/-
compensation is fixed on the owner and insurer of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-05-AF-4666 due to the contributory negligence. But owner and insurer of Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-AF-4666 are not parties to the petition. Hence petitioner is not entitled for award amount of 15% i.e.,
Rs.80,580/- Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative. 
ISSUE NO.3:
37. In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost. 
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,56,621/- (Rupees four lakh fifty six thousand six hundred twenty one only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount. 
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order. 
The compensation awarded to the future medication i.e., Rs.25,500/- shall not carry any interest.

9 After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years. And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-. 
Draw award accordingly. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 13th day of December 2024). 
(DHANESH MUGALI) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, MEMBER MACT & ACJM,
BENGALURU.
